messages:
nina_privacy: Heads up: Received a DSAR from an EU account asking for deletion of conversational logs + embeddings. Customer says they rotated their CMK last month (projects/customer-202/locations/global/keyRings/alpha/cryptoKeys/key-v2). They also asked for a proof-of-delete package.

sam_legal: Key points: verify identity (account_id + session proof or signed portal token). If key was rotated, confirm whether old ciphertext was re-encrypted or left as-is. Also check legal_hold tag in CRM.

own_sre: Quick tech note: our backup snapshots include objects encrypted with both key-v1 and key-v2 depending on snapshot date. We do not hold Decrypt on customer CMKs normally. Without decrypt we can't inspect or scrub blob contents, but we can delete object metadata / object itself in GCS if we have storage.objects.delete.

town: (ops-bot) Auto-check: CRM legal_hold flag: false. Backups list: gs://eu-chat-backups/2025-01-12-snap, gs://eu-chat-backups/2025-03-02-snap. Vector index shard ids: vec-eu-001, vec-eu-022.

tasha_engsec: Proposal to minimize blast radius: 1) Portal-auth verification issues one-time signed token (15m), 2) Create ephemeral job pod that mounts a kms-ephemeral-service-account via workload identity binding, with cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt scoped to the specific cryptoKey resource(s), 3) Job deletes index entries via vectorservice API and issues GCS delete for snapshot objects, 4) All actions annotated with dsar_id and job_id in audit events.

li_platform: Need RBAC details in the PR: define role roles/redwood.ephemeral_dsar_executor with precise permissions: storage.objects.delete, cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt on resource list, vector.indexEntries.delete. Add IAM Conditions: resource.name.startsWith("projects/customer-202/") && request.auth.claims.dsar_id == "dsar-2025-04-04-01" && request.time < timestamp("2025-04-05T00:00:00Z").

own_sre: Edge case: If key-v1 was destroyed by customer (DESTROY_SCHEDULED or DESTROYED) we won't be able to decrypt even with grant. In that case we can still delete raw blobs by object delete. But embeddings inside managed index that are encrypted server-side may require index compaction or re-encryption pass.

sam_legal: For proof-of-delete, we should produce: list of object paths deleted, vector-index shard IDs touched, audit log slice (with dsar_id, actor, timestamps), and KMS operation logs showing Decrypt calls (if any). Keep that evidence for 2 years as per retention policy.

tasha_engsec: Ops procedure addition: if Decrypt calls are made against customer CMK, capture the cryptoKey resource and KMS response code in the evidence bundle. If Decrypt denied -> annotate and escalate to infra-sec.

kms-bot: KMS Access Request created: KMS-ACCESS-2217 for projects/customer-202. Requested by tasha_engsec for ephemeral role.

li_platform: I'll add an audit schema change to include dsar_id, job_id, customer_id, cryptoKey_resource, and operation_result. Plan to deploy audit consumer by EOD tomorrow; we must not run deletion before consumer is live.

nina_privacy: Action owners: tasha_engsec -> IAM role PR and ephemeral job template, owen_sre -> runbook for failure modes & compaction, li_platform -> audit schema + consumer, sam_legal -> evidence retention rules and DSAR reply wording. ETA: role PR today, runbook + audit consumer by EOD next day.

ops-bot: Infra PR: infra/iam#4401 opened (adds roles/redwood.ephemeral_dsar_executor).

li_platform: Reminder: add dsar_id header to all internal erase API calls: "X-DSAR-ID: dsar-2025-04-04-01" so downstream services can correlate.

nina_privacy: I'll reply to requester with portal link to confirm identity and an estimated timeline. Will block final deletion until audit consumer confirms ingestion. Thanks all. :handshake:
